summary: Step 6 (PLUGINS) DONE - Hybrid Plugin Core + Ports. All approved corrections are implemented. (1) Registry != runtime policy: PluginRegistry.register(capability, name, instance) accepts ANY number of named adapters per capability (verified with worker: cline+codex, notifier: windows+email, reporting: markdown+excel, judge: claude-opus+other-judge, advisor: openai+claude+grok, and even storage: sqlite+in-memory). Active selection is separate and explicit via set_default(capability, name) / get_default(capability) / default_name(capability); the first registered adapter becomes the deterministic default, later registrations never steal it, and the default can be changed without re-registering. (2) CostPort widened to a stable contract: record(CostRecord) -> None plus query(CostQuery) -> CostSummary. CostQuery carries optional project / step_no / provider / from_time / to_time (all None = unfiltered), which covers total, today (a from_time/to_time window), by project, by step and by provider through one shape, and it ships a deterministic matches(record) predicate so adapters aggregate consistently. CostSummary reports total_usd, input_tokens, output_tokens and record_count. Step 16 can implement the cost plugin without rebuilding the core port. (3) WorkerPort is provider-neutral: WorkerRequest(task, context) DTO in, and WorkerResult(status: ReportStatus, summary, artifacts, issues, architecture_questions, raw: Optional[Mapping]) out - a minimal frozen value object with deterministic JSON-safe to_dict(); WorkerPort knows nothing about Cline (Step 7 will parse the Cline-specific format into this shape). (4) StoragePort approved as designed: repository ports stay separate, TransactionPort is NOT duplicated (StoragePort inherits TransactionPort, so exactly one transaction contract exists), StoragePort is a pure typed facade (nine repository accessors + transaction, zero business logic), and SqliteStorage is the single Step 6 infrastructure adapter composing the already-tested Sqlite* adapters plus SqliteTransactionPort over one connection. A test asserts the facade exposes no method other than transaction() and that rollback/commit/nesting behave exactly like the Step 5 boundary. (5) PluginCapability is a stable 7-value enum; plugin loading is explicit and deterministic with no filesystem scanning and no dynamic import - the registry module is asserted to contain no sqlite3/infrastructure/provider references. (6) The rest is as approved. Core ports vs concrete adapters stay cleanly separated: WorkerPort->Step 7, AdvisorPort->Steps 11-13, JudgePort->Step 15, CostPort->Step 16, ReportingPort->Step 20, NotifierPort->later, StoragePort->SqliteStorage (this step). No Cline/OpenAI/Claude/Grok implementations, no orchestrator/scheduler, no UI. VERIFICATION: python -m pytest -q -> 797 passed, 0 failed (117 new tests: 58 capability ports/DTOs, 30 plugin core registry, 29 storage facade). The Step 4 architecture self-check still passes: 26 modules, 0 violations, compliant; sqlite3 is imported only by infrastructure modules and ports/application import no infrastructure. One deliberate naming deviation: CostPort.query's parameter is named cost_filter instead of filter to avoid shadowing the builtin - the contract is identical. Also corrected a docstring claim during implementation: StoragePort IS runtime-checkable because it inherits TransactionPort, and isinstance(SqliteStorage(...), StoragePort) is True while requiring exactly the nine accessors plus transaction.
